This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 17.06.2023 at about 11.15 a.m. he had been walking on left side near SGT Railway Goods Shed, Bengaluru, at that time, a Ashok Leyland bearing Reg.
No.KA-08-6335
being driven by its driver came at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against him, due to the said impact, he fell down and sustained severe injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to MTB Orthopaedic & Trauma Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and he has spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical and travelling expenses.
SCCH-5 3.

At the time of the accident he was aged about 45 years, hale and healthy, working as coolie,
thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m., due to this accident he has suffered great mental shock, pain and suffering and unable to discharge his daily activities, he has lost his future life and became permanently disabled.

Out of this accident crime No.19/2023 is registered against the driver of the said lorry before the Cantonment Railway Police Station for the offences punishable under Sec.279,
338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the R.C.Owner, respondent No.2 is insurer of the said lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.30,00,000/-.

sentences.text: On service of notice, respondent No.1 /owner has not appeared before the court, hence placed exparte.
SCCH-5
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement.
Further admitted issuance of insurance policy in respect of lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-08-6335 and liability to indemnify respondent No.2 is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Respondent No.2 is entitled to take defence available under Sec.147 and 149(2) of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further submitted that there is lapse of 2 days in lodging complaint and petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties, as the driver of the lorry was also necessary party for the adjudication of the claim.
Further submitted that, driver of the offending lorry was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Further the said offending vehicle was not having valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.
Further denied age, SCCH-5 occupation and income of the petitioner.
Compensation claimed by the petitioner is on higher side.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 17.05.2023 at about 11.15 a.m. near SGT Railway Goods Shed, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent driving of Ashok Leyland Vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-08-6335 and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Medical Record SCCH-5 Incharge at MTB Orthopaedic & Trauma Hospital as PW-2, Dr.Nagaraj B.N.
Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS as PW-3 and marked 18 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no evidence of respondents.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:

sentences.text: Issue No.1:- In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts SCCH-5 averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of MLC is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.8.
9.
Further to substantiate petitioner case, he has examined Medical Record Incharge and Doctor as PW-2 and PW-3.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 and records those have marked i.e., FIR,
complaint, MLC, mahazar, seizure mahazar, sketch, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 17.06.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
SCCH-5 10.

Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 17.06.2023 at about 11.15 a.m. when he was walking on left side of SGT Railway Goods Shed,
Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
11. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the Ashok Leyland bearing Reg. No.KA-08-6335.

Under such SCCH-5 circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained fracture of right femur,
degloving injury over left knee, for which he has underwent surgeries in the form of close reduction IM nailing and debrideement and sutureing.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.13, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.9 issued by MTB Orthopaedic &
Trauma Hospital, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient from 17.06.2023 to 26.06.2033, once again from 03.07.2023 to 06.07.2023 and from 08.12.2023 to 14.12.2023 i.e., for 18 days.
SCCH-5

Further he has exhibited progress report marked as Ex.P.10, medical bills amounting to Rs.2,15,311/- marked as Ex.P.11.
13.

Further Medical Record Incharge in MTB Orthopaedic & Trauma Hospital by name Srinath is examined as PW-2, who has exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.P.14, copy of MLC intimation is marked as Ex.P.15, IP Case sheets are marked as Ex.P.16.

sentences.text: Further Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS is examined as PW-3.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited clinical notes marked as Ex.P.17 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.18 and he has assessed physical disability of the right lower limb at 48% and total physical disability of left lower limb at 32% and whole body disability at the rate of 25%.
In cross- SCCH-5 examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner and further deposed that, fractures are united, implants are insitu and degloving injury is healed.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 25% i.e., 1/3rd to the physical disability of right lower limb out of 48% and physical disability of left lower limb at 32%, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

15. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 45 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.12, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as SCCH-5 01.01.1978 and the alleged accident is occurred on 17.05.2023, accordingly relying on Ex.P.12 his age is considered about 46 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 13 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s.
Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.15,250/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose SCCH-5 of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

So as per Ex.P.13 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained fracture of right femur,
degloving injury over left knee, which are grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Ashok Kumar for the offences SCCH-5 punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 clearly states that,
petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
19.
Per contra except denial in the written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of them to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.

20. Ofcourse during the course of arguments, the learned counsel of respondent No.2 Sri.TR argued that, SCCH-5 there is no zebra cross in the place of accident, though petitioner has attempted to cross the road and as per sketch, accident was held in middle of the road and all injuries are healed and there is no disability to the petitioner etc., but said arguments are not support the respondent case in any manner, because they have not proved.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical bills and other compensation as stated below.
21. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl.No.

Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Future Income 5,94,750-00 2.
Pain and sufferings 15,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 2,15,311-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 6.
Loss of income during laid up 9,150-00 period Total 8,64,211-00 SCCH-5 22.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.8,64,211/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

23. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.
1-2Q5Z4KIL which is valid for the period from 14.03.2023 to 13.03.2024, the alleged accident was occurred on 17.06.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that, respondent Krishna Sahani vs Naveen Kumar Naryana on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16190701/

::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,64,211/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs Sixty Four Thousand Two Hundred Eleven Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.

The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
SCCH-5 Draw award accordingly.
